title: She never screamed.
paragraphs: In the quiet corners of 1 Samuel, there’s a woman most people read past too quickly.

And her pain?
It didn’t look loud.
It looked… invisible.
Year after year, she walked into the house of God carrying the same unanswered prayer.

A closed womb.
A wounded heart.
A soul drowning in silent questions.
But here’s what makes it heavier—
Targeted by someone who had what she desperately longed for.

Not to perform.
Not to impress.
But to pour out.

No polished words.
No religious script.
Just raw, shaking honesty before God.
The priest thought she was drunk.
Broken… and misjudged at the same time.
God heard what nobody else could.
Because God listens to what pain cannot say out loud.
“Lord, if You give me a son… I will give him back to You.”
But it all started with a woman…
Who chose to trust God in silence.
Your unanswered prayer is not ignored.
Your silent tears are not wasted.
Your hidden pain is not unseen.
Hannah didn’t just need a child.
Because the real struggle isn’t just external.

Sin separates us.
Pride hardens us.
Control exhausts us.
He steps into our silent struggles.
He carries what we cannot fix.
He redeems what we thought was dead.
Through the cross, He answers the deeper cry of the soul:
So if you feel unseen today…
You are standing exactly where Hannah once stood.

Reflection:
What silent burden have you been carrying that you haven’t truly surrendered to God?
This isn’t the end of your story.
